statement: The supplied sources contain no derivation. The Jacobian-vector product is defined as the directional derivative y' = \nabla f(x) \cdot x' \in \mathbb{R}^m of a differentiable function f: \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}^m at a point x \in \mathbb{R}^n in the direction x' \in \mathbb{R}^n, where \nabla f(x) denotes the Jacobian matrix of first-order partial derivatives of f evaluated at x.

symbols.meaning: Jacobian matrix of first-order partial derivatives of f evaluated at x
dual number pair representing primal value u and derivative/perturbation u'

properties.property: The Jacobian-vector product y' = \nabla f(x) \cdot x' can be computed simultaneously with the function value via dual number arithmetic as (\langle y_1, y'_1 \rangle, \ldots, \langle y_m, y'_m \rangle) = f(\langle x_1, x'_1 \rangle, \ldots, \langle x_n, x'_n \rangle).
properties.why: Adopting the directional derivative operator on dual numbers evaluates derivatives by repeatedly applying the chain rule to elementary operations without computing symbolic derivatives.

properties.property: To recover all elements of the full Jacobian matrix \nabla f, exactly n directional derivative (function) evaluations are required.
properties.why: Each directional derivative evaluation computes the Jacobian contracted against a single direction vector x'.

properties.property: The Jacobian matrix J_f(x) is the matrix of all first-order partial derivatives of f, generalizing the derivative and differential of a univariate function to vector-valued functions of several variables.
properties.why: Its entries are given by the partial derivatives of each component function f_i with respect to each coordinate x_j.

assumptions.assumption: The vector-valued function f: \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}^m is differentiable at x.
assumptions.breaks_when: The function contains non-differentiable operations or points where partial derivatives do not exist.

assumptions.assumption: The direction vector x' lies in the same domain space \mathbb{R}^n as the input x.
assumptions.breaks_when: The dimensions of the direction vector x' and input point x do not match.

failure_modes.mode: Division by zero in dual number arithmetic
failure_modes.signature: Undefined value or divide-by-zero error in (u'v - uv') / v^2
failure_modes.cause: A divisor argument evaluates to v = 0 in the primitive division rule.

failure_modes.mode: Logarithm domain violation in dual arithmetic
failure_modes.signature: Undefined derivative u'/u or arithmetic domain error
failure_modes.cause: The primal argument satisfies u <= 0, violating the u > 0 requirement for log.

failure_modes.mode: Non-differentiability of power or absolute value at zero
failure_modes.signature: Discontinuous sign function or undefined derivative in u' sgn(u)
failure_modes.cause: The primal argument u = 0, where absolute value and negative/fractional powers fail to be differentiable.

failure_modes.signature: Rank of the Jacobian matrix is not maximal (or Jacobian determinant vanishes when m = n)
failure_modes.cause: The evaluation point x is a critical point of f where all minors of maximal rank vanish.

canon_notes: canon expects a derivation but no source performs one, so jacobian_vector_product is recorded as a definition
